alt: Exercise 3.2 · Q8: In a group of 380 employees, 250 can speak Urdu, 150 can speak English, 50 can speak Punjabi, 40 can speak Urdu and English, 30 can speak both English and Punjabi, and 10 can speak Urdu and Punjabi. How many can speak all three languages?

steps.title: Set up
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\text{(assumption: each of the }380\text{ employees speaks at least one of the three languages)}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Result
steps.text: \[\begin{aligned}&\text{Let }U_{s}=\text{ Urdu speakers, }E=\text{ English}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{speakers, }P=\text{ Punjabi speakers}\\[5pt]&n(U_{s}\cup E\cup \text{ P) }=380,n(U_{s})=250,\\[5pt]&\quad \text{n(E) }=150,\text{ n(P) }=50\\[5pt]&n(U_{s}\cap \text{ E) }=40,\text{ n(E }\cap \text{ P) }=30,\\[5pt]&\quad n(U_{s}\cap \text{ P) }=10\\[5pt]&n(U_{s}\cup E\cup \text{ P) }=n(U_{s})+\text{ n(E) }+\text{ n(P)}\\[5pt]&\quad -n(U_{s}\cap \text{ E) }-\text{ n(E }\cap \text{ P) }-n(U_{s}\cap \text{ P) }+\\[5pt]&\quad n(U_{s}\cap E\cap \text{ P)}\\[5pt]&380=250+150+50-40-30-10+\\[5pt]&\quad \text{x}\\[5pt]&380=450-80+x\\[5pt]&380=370+x\\[5pt]&\therefore x=10\\[5pt]&\therefore \text{ }\textcolor{#047857}{\mathbf{10}}\text{ employees can speak all three}\\[5pt]&\quad \text{languages.}\end{aligned}\]
